Sloths can hold their breath underwater for up to 40 minutes by slowing down their heart rate, which is longer than a dolphin can!
If you could drive your car straight up into the sky at highway speed, you would reach outer space in just about one hour.
An average fluffy cumulus cloud looks completely weightless, but it actually weighs about 1.1 million pounds—the equivalent of roughly 100 elephants floating in the air!
The eye of a giant squid can grow up to thirty centimetres in diameter, which is about the same size as a dinner plate.
The Eiffel Tower can grow up to fifteen centimetres taller during the summer. This happens because the high temperatures cause the metal structure to expand.
Certain species of bamboo can grow up to ninety-one centimetres in a single day, making it the fastest-growing plant on Earth.
If you unraveled all the DNA inside your body, it would stretch for about sixty billion kilometres. This is long enough to travel from Earth to Pluto and back five times.
There is enough gold inside the core of the Earth to cover the entire surface of the planet in a layer that is forty-five centimetres deep.

The planet Venus rotates so slowly on its axis that a single day there lasts longer than an entire Venusian year. It takes Venus two hundred and forty-three Earth days to complete one rotation, but only two hundred and twenty-five Earth days to orbit the Sun.
The peregrine falcon is the fastest animal on Earth, reaching speeds of over three hundred and twenty kilometres per hour when diving through the air.
A giraffe has a dark blue tongue that can grow up to fifty centimetres long, which protects it from sunburn while it eats leaves high in the trees.
The howler monkey is the loudest land animal on Earth, and its deep call can be heard clearly from a distance of up to five kilometres away.
The heart of a blue whale is about the size of a small car and weighs around one hundred and eighty kilograms.
A puffin can flap its wings up to four hundred times per minute, allowing it to fly at speeds of eighty-eight kilometres per hour.

To gather enough nectar to make just one kilogram of honey, honeybees must fly a total distance of nearly two hundred thousand kilometres, which is equivalent to travelling around the Earth five times.
The ancient Maya used cacao beans, the main ingredient in chocolate, as a form of currency to buy goods and services.
Ancient Egyptians enjoyed playing board games, and one of their favorites was a game called Senet. It was so popular that people from all levels of society, including pharaohs, played it.
The small dot over the lowercase letters i and j is called a tittle.
An octopus has three hearts, and its blood is naturally blue.
There is no historical evidence that Vikings ever wore horned helmets into battle, as this idea was created by costume designers during the nineteenth century.
Because the Moon has no atmosphere, there is no wind or water to wash away the footprints left behind by astronauts, meaning they will last for millions of years.
Sea otters hold paws while they sleep to keep from drifting apart in the water.
The Pacific Ocean is so vast that it covers more area than all of the Earth's landmasses combined.
Human babies are born with about three hundred bones, but many of these fuse together as they grow. By adulthood, the human body has only two hundred and six bones.
The first computer mouse, invented in the 1960s, was carved out of wood and had just a single button.
